findings.title: Team admin/owner permission check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, so a caller must be both admin and owner. A team admin who is not the owner fails the check and gets FORBIDDEN, even though the UI shows the 'additional guests' action to them. The intended check is an OR of the two conditions.

findings.title: Guest blacklist comparison is case-sensitive on the guest side
findings.body: The blacklist entries are lowercased on line 71, but the incoming `guest` is compared as typed (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). Submitting `Spam@Example.com` bypasses a blacklist entry `spam@example.com`, which defeats the abuse control the env var exists for.

findings.title: Guests array has no size limit; any attendee can mass-mail arbitrary addresses
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no max length and no per-user rate limit. Each new guest receives a calendar invite and an email containing booking details, and the handler also sends an email to every existing attendee. Any authenticated user who is merely an attendee (the handler allows `isAttendee`) can send a single request with thousands of addresses to third parties through the platform's mail infrastructure, with no cap.

findings.title: Duplicate guests in one request, or case-variant duplicates, create duplicate attendee rows
findings.body: The filter on lines 74-78 only removes guests already present in `booking.attendees` (exact, case-sensitive match). It does not dedupe within `guests` itself, and the server schema does not enforce uniqueness, so the same email sent twice passes and both copies go into `createMany` on line 102. Case variants such as `Bob@x.com` and `bob@x.com` are also both inserted. The result is duplicate attendee rows and duplicate invites. The uniqueness rule is enforced only in the client dialog.

findings.title: Guests are persisted before calendar sync, and calendar failure is unhandled
findings.body: The attendees are written to the DB at lines 92-106. `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` at line 165 is not wrapped in try/catch, unlike the email call. If the calendar update throws, the request fails after the guests were saved, and no invites are sent. A retry then hits the dedupe check on lines 74-81 and returns BAD_REQUEST, so the user cannot recover without manual DB cleanup. The writes should be ordered or wrapped so that a calendar failure does not leave persisted guests with no invite.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` returns the calling user's credentials, and the `EventManager` is built from them. When a team admin or an attendee (not the organizer) adds guests, the calendar event belongs to the organizer's connected calendar, so `updateCalendarAttendees` runs against the wrong account's credentials and either fails or does not update the organizer's event. The organizer's credentials are loaded on line 38 (`booking.user.credentials`) but never used.

findings.title: No check on booking status or time; guests can be added to cancelled or past bookings
findings.body: After the booking is loaded, the handler only checks existence and permissions. It never checks whether the booking is cancelled or rejected, or whether it has ended. A direct API call can add attendees and send calendar invites for a cancelled booking, which effectively reactivates it on the guest's calendar. The UI hides this action for cancelled bookings, but the server does not enforce it.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores eventType disableStandardEmails metadata
findings.body: Every other send function in this file gates host and attendee emails on `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and always sends to organizers, team members, and attendees. The handler also does not pass the event type metadata. Organizers who disabled standard emails for this event type will still receive add-guest emails.

findings.title: Existing attendees who were re-submitted get the new-booking email
findings.body: The handler passes the raw `guests` input (line 168 of addGuests.handler.ts) instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`. Here, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` therefore matches existing attendees who were in the request, and they receive a full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the 'guests added' notice. The function should receive only the newly created guests.

findings.title: Email failure is logged with console.log and the error object is dropped
findings.body: The catch block logs the constant string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' and discards `err`, so the failure cause is unrecoverable from logs. It should use the project logger and include the error. Swallowing the error is intentional, but the diagnostic detail should not be lost.

findings.title: Misleading error when all guests are already attendees or blacklisted
findings.body: When every submitted guest is already an attendee or on the blacklist, the handler throws BAD_REQUEST with message 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' ('Emails must be unique and valid'). That message does not explain the real cause. Blacklisted addresses are dropped silently, and the user is told their emails are invalid even when they are valid and simply already present.

findings.title: Error toast shows raw error code, and the fallback is dead code
findings.body: `message` is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, which always yields a non-empty string, so `message || t('unable_to_add_guests')` on line 44 never uses the fallback. The user sees raw tRPC codes such as 'FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission'. If `err.data` is missing, the toast starts with 'undefined:'. The toast should show the translated message, with the fallback used when it is absent.

findings.title: Validation error flag is never cleared, so it persists after the user fixes input
findings.body: `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is called on validation failure, but it is only reset by the Cancel button. After a successful add, or after the dialog is closed via the overlay or X button, the 'Emails must be unique and valid' message is still shown the next time the dialog opens. The flag should be cleared on success and on open/close.

findings.title: Hardcoded English tooltip text is not translated
findings.body: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">` is a hardcoded English string in a shared UI component that elsewhere uses `t(...)` for all user-facing text (for example the 'Add another' button). Non-English users see English here, so it should use a translation key added to common.json.

findings.title: No tests for a new permission-gated mutation with dedupe and email logic
findings.body: The PR adds a mutation with authorization rules (organizer, team admin/owner, attendee), blacklist and duplicate filtering, calendar sync, and email fan-out, but no unit or integration tests. The permission `&&` bug and the duplicate-insertion problem would likely be caught by even basic tests of the handler's branches.
